title: Alentejo & Costa Vicentina Gravel

bestPeriod.avoid: July-August, inland Alentejo regularly exceeds 40°C with no shade on the montado, and coastal accommodation triples in price

accommodation.note: Évora and Monsaraz €80, €140 pppn; coastal guesthouses €70, €120

food.note: Tasca mains €10, €16; a Milfontes seafood dinner €30, €45

transport.note: Airport transfers, one Odemira-line train leg, luggage shuttle

activities.note: Gravel hire €180, €260/week (usually delivered), Alqueva stargazing session €25

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5, moderate gradients but long, exposed, low-traffic days with heavy gravel resistance and real water-carrying discipline

gatewayAirport: LIS Lisbon Humberto Delgado, 1 h 30 min to Évora; FAO Faro, 1 h 45 min to Mértola and 2 h to Vila Nova de Milfontes
summary: The Alentejo is Europe's emptiest agricultural landscape and its gravel is correspondingly generous, hundreds of kilometres of hard clay and schist farm track winding through montado, the cork-oak savannah that has been managed the same way for eight centuries. This week runs from Évora's Roman and Manueline core east to the walled hilltop of Monsaraz above the Alqueva reservoir, south through Mértola's Islamic castle to the Guadiana, then west to the Atlantic, where the Costa Vicentina delivers cliffs, storks nesting on sea stacks, and a headwind that defines the last two days. It is a route about space, silence and heat management rather than climbing, and it needs a rider comfortable being 30 km from the nearest café.

itinerary.title: Évora, and the first montado tracks
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Évora, take delivery of the gravel bike, and walk the walled centre: the Roman Templo de Diana, the Sé cathedral roof terrace, and the Capela dos Ossos with its wall of monastic bones.
itinerary.afternoon: A short shakedown east through the Herdade da Mitra estate tracks and the Valverde area, past the Cromeleque dos Almendres, a 95-stone Neolithic circle older than Stonehenge, reached on 3 km of rough gravel.
itinerary.evening: Botequim da Mouraria on Rua da Mouraria, nine counter seats, no reservations, exceptional Alentejo cooking. If it is full, Fialho on Travessa das Mascarenhas is the classic alternative.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km / 460 m ascent / 55% clay track, 45% paved / Almendres access 3 km unsurfaced

itinerary.title: Évora to Monsaraz across the plain
itinerary.morning: East out of Évora on the empty N254 toward Reguengos de Monsaraz, dropping onto estate tracks at São Manços. This is textbook montado: cork oaks stripped to red trunks, black pigs, no shade at head height.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach the Alqueva shore and climb the 2.1 km ramp to Monsaraz's Porta da Vila, finishing on cobbles at 14%. The walled village is a single street and a castle keep, with the reservoir filling the whole eastern horizon.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Sabores de Monsaraz inside the walls, then an Alqueva Dark Sky session, this was the world's first Starlight Tourism Destination and the observatory at Cumeada runs guided sessions.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 690 m ascent / 50% clay track, 40% paved, 10% cobbles / Monsaraz 232 m, max 14%
itinerary.sleep: São Lourenço do Barrocal, near Monsaraz

itinerary.title: The Alqueva montado circuit
itinerary.morning: The signature gravel day: a loop through São Marcos do Campo, Motrinos and Telheiro on estate tracks, with the Alqueva reservoir appearing and disappearing between oaks. Water at Motrinos; there is nothing else for 25 km.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to the reservoir at Telheiro for a swim, then the last climb back to Monsaraz. Total ascent is modest but the clay resistance makes the effort feel 30% higher than the numbers.
itinerary.evening: Eat at São Lourenço do Barrocal's own restaurant, the estate's produce, its own wines, and a terrace looking at the same hill you rode all day.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 780 m ascent / 70% clay estate track, 25% paved, 5% cobbles / longest waterless stretch 25 km
itinerary.sleep: São Lourenço do Barrocal, near Monsaraz

itinerary.title: South to Mértola and the Guadiana
itinerary.morning: Transfer south past Serpa, or ride the long option through Vidigueira and Vila de Frades, the region of talha wine, still fermented in clay amphorae, which you can taste at Herdade do Rocim.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride into Mértola on the Guadiana schist ramps. The town is a stack of white houses under a Moorish castle, and its mosque-turned-church retains the mihrab, one of very few in Portugal.
itinerary.evening: Tamuje, on the riverbank below the castle, for Guadiana fish and Alentejo black pork.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km ridden / 820 m ascent / 45% schist track, 55% paved / repeated 1.5-3 km ramps at 6-8%
itinerary.sleep: Casa Amarela or the Hotel Museu, Mértola

itinerary.title: Guadiana valley to the Atlantic
itinerary.morning: North-west through the Vale do Guadiana Natural Park on schist tracks toward Castro Verde, an ochre landscape of open steppe that is one of Europe's most important great bustard habitats.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue toward Odemira. This is the transition day and the N120 corridor is the obvious line, treat it with caution: it is narrow, has no hard shoulder, carries heavy timber and eucalyptus trucks, and is genuinely unpleasant to ride. Use the parallel municipal roads and the Rota Vicentina signed gravel wherever they exist, even at the cost of 15 km.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Vila Nova de Milfontes. Tasca do Celso on Rua dos Aviadores is the town's institution, book, or eat at 19:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 96 km / 1,010 m ascent / 40% schist and clay track, 60% paved / N120 exposure minimised to under 8 km
itinerary.sleep: HS Milfontes Beach Hotel, Vila Nova de Milfontes

itinerary.title: Costa Vicentina: Almograve, Cabo Sardão, Zambujeira
itinerary.morning: South from Milfontes on the coastal lanes and signed Rota Vicentina cycling routes to Almograve, then Cavaleiro and the Cabo Sardão lighthouse, where white storks nest on the sea stacks, the only place in the world they nest on ocean cliffs.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue on hardpack and sand to Zambujeira do Mar. Remember the cliff-edge Fishermen's Trail here is walking-only; the parallel gravel and municipal lanes are the legal cycling line.
itinerary.evening: O Sacas at Entrada da Barca below Zambujeira, a shack above the fishing cove serving whatever came in that morning.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 620 m ascent / 45% hardpack, 35% paved, 20% loose sand / Fishermen's Trail closed to bikes
itinerary.sleep: Herdade do Touril, Zambujeira do Mar

itinerary.title: Cork country and the ride out
itinerary.morning: Inland loop east from Zambujeira through São Teotónio and the cork estates toward Odemira, on the best clay tracks of the week. Watch for freshly stripped cork oaks numbered with the year of harvest, they are cut once every nine years.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the bike to the delivery operator at Odemira or Zambujeira, then transfer to Faro or Lisbon.
itinerary.evening: If you have time in Lisbon, eat in Cais do Sodré before the flight; otherwise a final grilled fish at Milfontes harbour.
itinerary.dayStats: 54 km / 560 m ascent / 65% clay track, 35% paved / transfer to FAO 1 h 45 min
itinerary.sleep: Herdade do Touril, or an airport hotel

accommodationStrategy.name: São Lourenço do Barrocal
accommodationStrategy.description: A 200-year-old monte turned hotel on 780 hectares, with secure bike storage, its own fleet for guests, a wine cellar producing on site, and direct access to estate gravel tracks from the door. Expensive at roughly €280, €420 double, but it is the only property that lets you ride the Alqueva circuit without touching a public road for the first 8 km.

accommodationStrategy.name: Convento do Espinheiro
accommodationStrategy.description: A fifteenth-century convent 3 km from Évora's walls, with a lockable cloister storeroom for bikes and a pool that matters after a 40°C day. Positioned on the eastern side, so you leave toward Monsaraz without crossing the city. Around €150, €230 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Herdade do Touril
accommodationStrategy.description: A working farm on the cliff edge with a bike outbuilding, an outdoor hose, and a private path down to the beach. Breakfast is served early enough for a pre-wind coastal start, which is the single most valuable feature on the Costa Vicentina. €120, €190 double.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is reasonable in towns and along the coast, but there are real dead zones in the Guadiana valley and on interior estates. Portugal is in the EU so roaming applies. Download offline maps: many estate tracks are gated and unmapped, and gates in the montado are often locked without notice.
logistics.emergency: 112. Portugal honours EHIC/GHIC. The nearest full hospitals are in Évora, Beja and Faro; the Costa Vicentina's nearest is at Odemira health centre with transfers to Beja. Response times in the interior can exceed an hour, carry a satellite messenger if riding solo on estate tracks.
logistics.weather: The nortada, a persistent north-westerly Atlantic wind, blows almost every afternoon on the coast from April to September, frequently at 30-45 km/h. Ride south, and ride early. Inland the risk is heat, not wind, a 40°C day on unshaded clay is genuinely dangerous. Coastal fog (nevoeiro) can cut visibility on the cliff lanes at dawn.
logistics.bookingWindows: São Lourenço do Barrocal books three to six months for spring. Coastal guesthouses fill entirely in August. Delivered rental bikes need four weeks. Botequim da Mouraria does not take bookings and seats nine, arrive at opening. Alqueva stargazing sessions need a few days.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted in towns; rural tascas and village cafés in the Guadiana valley are frequently cash-only, and ATMs are scarce between Mértola and Odemira. Tipping is 5-10% at a restaurant, rounding elsewhere.
logistics.transportRules: Portuguese motorway tolls on the A22 and parts of the A2 are electronic-only, a rental car needs a transponder or a registered plate. CP Regional and InterRegional trains carry bikes free in designated spaces; Alfa Pendular and Intercidades require bagging with limited bookable spaces. Rede Expressos coaches take boxed bikes at driver's discretion.
logistics.permits: The Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina restricts off-track riding, and the Fishermen's Trail is closed to bicycles. Cork oaks are legally protected trees, do not lean bikes on freshly stripped trunks, which are open wounds. Estate tracks cross private land under customary access; close every gate you open. Drones need ANAC registration and are restricted over the natural park.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable across the region but often heavily mineralised inland. Carry a minimum of three litres on montado days. Ticks are present in cork-oak scrub. Portuguese man o' war occasionally wash onto Costa Vicentina beaches on westerly swells. Sun exposure, not traffic, is the main medical risk on this route.

proTips: Ride the coast north to south. The nortada is a tailwind going south and a wall going north; the same 46 km leg can take two hours or four.
Do not plan any bike section on the Fishermen's Trail, however tempting the GPX looks. It is a walking route on erodible dune and cliff, and riding it is both prohibited and locally resented.
Start montado days at first light. The clay tracks are firm and cool before 10:00 and turn to dust-and-glare afterwards, and there is no shade to wait in.
Ask São Lourenço do Barrocal or your Évora hotel which estate gates are currently open. Locked farm gates are the most common route failure in the Alentejo and no map shows them.
Taste talha wine at Vila de Frades or Herdade do Rocim rather than in Évora. Clay-amphora Alentejo wine barely leaves its villages and the November talha season is when the pots are opened.
Carry two spare tubes and a tyre boot. Alentejo schist cuts sidewalls, and there is no bike shop between Évora and Odemira.
Book the Alqueva Dark Sky observatory session for a moonless night, the reservoir has among the lowest light pollution in Europe and the difference between new and full moon is total.
Use the Linha do Sul railheads at Funcheira or Ourique to skip the worst of the N120 if the transition day looks hot. CP Regional takes bikes free.
Cork harvest runs roughly May to August. Estate tracks in harvest see slow trucks and stacked bark, pass wide and expect diversions.

raw.Signature gravel day, the Alqueva montad: 74 km, 780 m ascent, on hard clay estate tracks between cork oaks with three short 12% pitches on the Monsaraz approach.
raw.Monsaraz wall ramp: 2.1 km at 6.4% from the Alqueva shore, maximum 14% on the final cobbled approach to Porta da Vila, summit 232 m. Short but it is the only meaningful gradient for 40 km in any direction.
raw.Serra de Serpa/Mértola schist climbs: the Guadiana valley delivers repeated 1.5-3 km ramps at 6-8% on broken schist, with the day's high point around 220 m, low numbers that mislead badly, because the surface is loose plate and the sun is unrelenting.
raw.Coastal leg, Vila Nova de Milfontes to Z: 46 km, 620 m ascent, on sand-over-hardpack and paved lanes via Almograve and Cavaleiro, with the Cabo Sardão lighthouse detour.
raw.Week surface split: approximately 45% hard clay and schist farm track, 30% paved (narrow, empty municipal roads), 15% loose sand on the coastal sections, 10% cobbled village setts. Run 45-50 mm tyres; anything narrower will bog in the Costa Vicentina sand.
raw.Rota Vicentina rules, read this before r: the Fishermen's Trail (Trilho dos Pescadores) is a walking route along cliff edge and dune and is not a cycling route; do not plan bike days on it. The Historical Way is the one long-distance Rota Vicentina route that has historically been open to cyclists, and the network now also publishes over 1,000 km of dedicated MTB and gravel trails across 38 signed routes in four difficulty grades, a 145 km long-distance MTB trail through the Odemira area with train-station connections, and a roughly 500 km touring route between Lisbon and Faro suited to gravel, hybrid and touring bikes. Use those, and treat cliff-edge singletrack as off-limits.
raw.Bike hire: local rental in the Alentejo interior is genuinely scarce, the practical model is a Lisbon operator such as Bike Iberia delivering gravel or touring bikes to Évora and collecting from the coast, at roughly €30, €40/day for a gravel bike and €160, €260/week including delivery, or booking through a Rota Vicentina bike-friendly partner in Odemira or São Teotónio. E-bike hire is easier to find on the coast than inland. One-way drop-off across the region is normal with delivery operators but should be priced at booking; bike-box storage is usually held by the operator in Lisbon, not locally.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: São Lourenço do Barrocal near Monsaraz has a secure bike store and its own bikes; Herdade do Touril at Zambujeira do Mar keeps bikes in a farm outbuilding with a hose; Convento do Espinheiro outside Évora will lock bikes in a cloister storeroom. Ask about a hose specifically, Alentejo clay dust in the drivetrain is the mechanical risk of the week.
raw.Bike on public transport: Comboios de Portugal carries bikes free on Regional and InterRegional services in designated spaces, subject to capacity; Alfa Pendular and Intercidades require the bike bagged or dismantled, with limited spaces bookable in advance. The Linha do Sul stops at Funcheira and Ourique are the useful railheads for the Odemira area. Rede Expressos coaches take boxed bikes in the hold for a fee at driver's discretion.

typeSpecific.surface: approximately 45% hard clay and schist farm track, 30% paved (narrow, empty municipal roads), 15% loose sand on the coastal sections, 10% cobbled village setts. Run 45-50 mm tyres; anything narrower will bog in the Costa Vicentina sand.

sources.verified: Rota Vicentina's own cycling page confirming that the Historical Way was the original route open to cyclists, that the network now publishes a dedicated bike offer of more than 1,000 km across 38 routes in four difficulty levels, a 145 km long-distance MTB trail in the Odemira area with train-station connections, and roughly 500 km of touring route between Lisbon and Faro for hybrid, gravel and touring bikes, plus a bike-friendly partner accommodation scheme. The Fishermen's Trail is presented as a walking route and is not offered as a cycling route.
sources.confidenceNotes: Rental logistics are the weakest point in this file, inland Alentejo hire is thin, and the named delivery model plus its indicative pricing must be confirmed with the operator before publishing. Whether cycling is formally prohibited or merely not offered on the Fishermen's Trail should be checked against current park regulations, as enforcement and signage have changed. Hotel rates for São Lourenço do Barrocal, Convento do Espinheiro and Herdade do Touril are prior-season estimates. Mértola accommodation names should be re-verified as trading. CP bike-carriage rules by service class and Rede Expressos coach policy need confirmation. The Alqueva Dark Sky observatory session format and price change seasonally. Cromeleque dos Almendres access-track condition varies after winter rain.
